Shrink a fitted model before saving it

Source: R/strip.R
strip_sdmTMB.Rd

Removes objects from a fitted model that sdmTMB rebuilds as needed, so the model takes less space when saved with saveRDS(). The stripped model works the same as one read back from disk: its objective function is taped again the first time a method needs it.

Usage

strip_sdmTMB(object, strip_joint_precision = FALSE)

Arguments

object

A model fit with sdmTMB().

strip_joint_precision

Also remove the joint precision matrix of the fixed and random effects? This usually gives the largest saving, but makes some methods slower. See Details.

Value

The fitted model with the removed objects.

Details

This removes the handle to the in-memory RTMB tape, which doesn't survive a save and reload and can be the largest part of a saved model, and the cached sparse Cholesky factor of the random-effects Hessian, which sdmTMB rebuilds cheaply when needed.

The joint precision matrix is often the largest part of what remains, but removing it (strip_joint_precision = TRUE) has a cost later:

  • Simulation-based methods (e.g., predict(..., nsim = ), get_index_sims(), spread_sims(), gather_sims(), and project()) recompute it with RTMB::sdreport() each time they are called. It isn't stored back in the model, so every call costs about as much as the sdreport() step of the original fit, which can take minutes for large spatiotemporal models.

  • get_index(), get_cog(), and get_eao() can't use a shortcut based on the matrix and instead build a new objective function and run RTMB::sdreport() on it.

Other methods (e.g., predict() without nsim, tidy(), and residuals()) are unaffected, as are models fit without the matrix (see get_joint_precision in sdmTMBcontrol()).

The original object is not changed.

Examples

mesh <- make_mesh(pcod_2011, c("X", "Y"), cutoff = 20)
fit <- sdmTMB(density ~ 1, data = pcod_2011, mesh = mesh,
  family = tweedie())
fit_small <- strip_sdmTMB(fit)
object.size(serialize(fit, NULL))
#> 4271816 bytes
object.size(serialize(fit_small, NULL))
#> 1099664 bytes
p <- predict(fit_small)
